newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end trade dulled by lack of impetus.
newsitem.headline: German shares end trade dulled by lack of impetus.

text.p: German shares ended a calm day's trade practically unchanged from opening levels, with any meaningful gains stifled by lacklustre investor activity in the wake of last week's record-breaking performance.
The IBIS DAX index, which gauges electronic trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks, ended the day at 2,654.34 points, down 1.15 points or 0.04 percent.
Earlier, the DAX index ended floor trade up 3.88 points at 2,655.73, having been well supported around the 2,640 level, dealers said, noting there was no concerted selling pressure.
"We are low on economic news, low on corporate news. This market is really still drawing breath after the push upward we had last week," said a Munich dealer.

The strengthening of the dollar over the afternoon did little to help boost interest in the market, and a neutral opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index also provided little inspiration to investors.
The prospect of Germany's public holiday on Thursday, which marks the country's unification, also kept activity low.

Stocks in the limelight included carmaker BMW AG which ended floor trade up five marks at 878.50 marks and ended the day up 3.85 marks at 876 marks after it announced an eight percent improvement in its nine-month unit car sales.
German chemical and metals group Degussa AG ended the floor trade up 16 marks at 568.50 marks after it forecast a doubling of sales growth over the next three years.
Degussa ended IBIS trade up 2.70 percent at 570 marks.
